in_text_mentions: Magnetic resonance spectroscopy of the frontal lobe mass only showed a lactate peak, which was non-specific and failed to establish the presence of a definite tumor signature. Excision biopsy of the right frontal lobe mass was immediately done. Histopathology was consistent with lymphoma revealing atypical large round blue cells with scant cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli. Immunohistochemical staining revealed that the tissue was positive for CD20 and negative for CD3, CAM 5.2, and glial fibrillary acidic protein (Figure 3) confirming the diagnosis of a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

panels.rationale: Single axial post-contrast MRI of the brain in a 70-year-old man shows a well-marginated 3.8 cm enhancing mass in the left frontal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema, confirmed by biopsy as high-grade B-cell lymphoma with no systemic disease (PCNSL). Caption and in-text explicitly attribute the lesion to primary CNS lymphoma; frontal lobe location with peritumoral edema is a classic PCNSL presentation, though the caption describes heterogeneous rather than the more typical homogeneous enhancement (recorded as a proposed finding since it is absent from the vocabulary).

A: Panel A shows CD20-positive B-cell lymphoma cells in a patient with primary central nervous system lymphoma/PTLD, a classic diagnostic immunohistochemical feature. [raw subtype: diffuse large B-cell lymphoma] B: Panel B shows CD10-negative staining in the same lymphoma, consistent with the non-germinal center immunophenotype typical of primary CNS lymphoma; the finding is not in the supplied vocabulary, so it is proposed. [raw subtype: diffuse large B-cell lymphoma] C: Panel C shows MUM-1-positive tumor cells, supporting the activated B-cell/non-germinal center phenotype of primary CNS lymphoma; MUM-1 is not in the supplied vocabulary, so it is proposed. [raw subtype: diffuse large B-cell lymphoma] D: Panel D shows BCL-6-positive tumor cells, an additional immunophenotypic marker supporting the diagnosis of primary CNS lymphoma; BCL-6 is not in the supplied vocabulary, so it is proposed. The biopsy was indicative of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (Figure 4).
